utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. On this Monday, I'd like to welcome the Prosecution that are in full number, and all the Defence counsel, and of course the accused, and everybody else in this courtroom. I'm going to start off by giving the floor to the registrar for some IC numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. Several parties have submitted lists of documents to be tendered through Witness Josip Praljak. OTP estimated in particular 14 lists, one for each bundle of documents. The first list -- the first bundle shall be assigned Exhibit number 454. The second bundle shall become Exhibit -- IC 455. The third bundle shall become Exhibit IC 456. The fourth bundle shall become Exhibit IC 457. Bundle number shall become Exhibit IC 458. Bundle number six shall become Exhibit IC 459. Bundle number seven shall become Exhibit IC 460. Bundle number eight shall become IC 461. Bundle number nine shall become Exhibit IC 462. Bundle number 10 shall become Exhibit IC 463. Bundle number 11 shall become Exhibit number IC 464. Bundle number 12 shall become Exhibit IC 465. Bundle number 13 shall become IC 466, while bundle number 14 shall become IC 467. The list submitted by 2D shall be given Exhibit number IC 468. The list submitted by 3D shall be given Exhibit number IC 369 [sic]. The list submitted by 5D shall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. The list submitted by 5D shall being Exhibit IC 470. While the list submitted by 6D shall be given Exhibit number IC 471. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. The Chamber has an oral decision to render regarding the exhibits presented during Witness CT's testimony and the witness appeared on the 11th of January, 2007. The Chamber has decided to admit into evidence exhibits presented by the Prosecution on the basis of list IC 0210, on the grounds that they present certain probative value and relevance. Let me repeat the number. IC 02102 -- 0210. The Chamber would like to note that Exhibits P 09805 and P 0880. Let me repeat the number P 0888 - three 8s - 0, are admitted into evidence under seal. Furthermore, the Chamber has decided to admit into evidence Exhibit P 02769 presented by the Stojic Defence and exhibit P 02749 presented by the Coric Defence on the grounds that they represent a certain probative value and relevance. I should also like to tell you, although you know this, that the Chamber rendered a ruling last week concerning the reduction of time that the Prosecution will have, and the Chamber maintains its decision, and I had an opinion apart that I set in -- forward my position with respect to the Chamber's opinions and the question of reduction of time. So the decision that we took reducing the time is fully upheld. Now, with respect to the witness that is going to appear today, we have decided that will the Prosecution will have six hours for the examination-in-chief, and six hours will be the maximum time allotted. Now, as to the Defence teams, the cross-examination will have the following amount of time: For the Prlic Defence, 60 minutes, a maximum of 60 minutes. Mr. Stojic will have 75 minutes, a maximum. Mr. Praljak will have 60 minutes, a maximum of 60 minutes. Mr. Coric will have a maximum of 75 minutes. Mr. Petkovic will have a maximum of 75 minutes, and the Pusic Defence will have a maximum of 60 minutes. Now, if all the Defence teams respect the time allotted, we should be over with the witness by Thursday. As -- well, we received a motion from the Defence on the 2nd of March regarding Josip Praljak who met someone in the month of August, so Mr. Pusic and his counsel, would they please tell us about this. Mr. Ibrisimovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'm try and explain the situation. On Friday -- on Friday, late in the afternoon, we received two more statements from the Prosecution with respect to this witness. We expected to receive an explanation of what we had heard later on -- earlier on, and on Friday evening I presented these statements to Mr. Pusic and asked him to give me a written statement about that. We've received the written statement. It is being translated, and I hope that we'll have a finished version by tomorrow and send in our request. Mr. Pusic did meet Mr. Praljak as the witness explained, but not in 2006 but much earlier on, so not in the summer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall be reading the written declaration and the filing very carefully. I'd just like to say that on page 3, line 16, when I said that we received requests, it was from the Prosecution, not the Defence. So that's the mistake there. We're now going to have the witness shown in, and I'm going to ask Madam Usher to go and fetch the witness. The Prosecution has prepared all these documents for us. We have a whole bunch of them. I don't know who is going to be taking the examination-in-chief. Mr. Mundis or Mr. Kruger?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will be conducting the direct examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. I'm going to start off by seeing if you can understand me in your own language and hear me. If so, tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On behalf of my colleagues and myself, I'd like to say good afternoon. As you know, you are a Prosecution witness called to testify here about certain facts or documents. Before you take the solemn declaration, I would like to ask you for your first name, last name, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Marijan Biskic. I was born on the 7th of February, 1959.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, what is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a retired officer of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're a retired officer. What rank did you have when you retired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was a brigadier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And you're not working at the moment? You're receiving a pension, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and I'm working in a private firm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what are you, a consultant or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a consultant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in what area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Integrated security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you ever testified before and international or national tribunal before on the events that took place in your country or is this the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you go ahead and read the solemn declaration now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give you some information first about the proceedings of the afternoon. As the Prosecutor has probably told you, because you met with the Prosecutor yesterday and this morning probably, and perhaps also on Saturday, I don't know, but you will be answering questions put to you by the Prosecutor, an and that in this says is Mr. Mundis, who will be presenting documents as well, which you probably looked through with him during the proofing session, as it's called. And for their -- the Prosecution's questions we have allotted a time of six hours, which would take us until tomorrow. After the examination-in-chief, it will it be turn of the Defence counsel and perhaps the accused as well. They will be asking you questions within what we call the cross-examination, and we have divided up the time amongst the Defence teams for the cross-examination and the Defence teams' questions, which means that we ought to finish your testimony by Thursday. The four Judges sitting up at the Bench in front of you may also ask you questions at all times. We're going to try and discipline ourselves and not to intervene unless it's absolutely necessary, and we'll ask our questions after the Prosecution has asked theirs to prevent interrupting the Prosecutor, unless there is an absolute necessity to do so. If we believe that the Prosecutor should have asked you a question which he did not, then we will step in. Do your best to be as precise as possible in your answers, and since you're an officer I have no concerns on that score. I'm sure you'll be able to answer the questions properly. If you don't understand a question, please don't hesitate to ask the person asking it to repeat it. If during the proceedings at any time you feel unwell, don't hesitate to let us know and we'll take a break, because I'm sure you'll find that answering questions over many hours and a number of days is a very exhausting process. So we will understand it if you would like to have a break. We have regular breaks every one and a half hours when we take a 20-minute break to allow you to have a rest and to allow the technical officers to change the tapes. If you need to address the Chamber at any time in the course of your testimony, feel free to do so. So that in very general terms it is how the proceedings are going to evolve. I'd just like to bring up a procedural point. You are a witness here, and a witness is required to answer questions, but if you consider that a question threatens to intimidate [as interpreted] you, then you need not answer the question. This is something that we never came across, but the Chamber can compel you to reply; but this will not be held against you in the proceedings. But rest assured that up until now we haven't found ourselves faced with the situation, but one never knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: A small direction to line 24 of page 7, threatens to incriminate and not "intimidate."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's not to intimidate, it is to incriminate, an answer that might incriminate you, not intimidate. Although the word intimidate is incorporated in the word incriminate but it's not the same thing, of course. Now, Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Brigadier Biskic?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to start by asking you some questions about your military career and background. Can you please tell the Chamber when you first joined any military force?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I joined in 1988 -- or, rather, from 1978 I was a member of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, in 1978 when you joined the JNA what -- in what capacity were you serving commencing in 1978?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: In 1978 I was -- I attended the first year of the military academy in Belgrade for the land forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, did you in fact complete the military academy in Belgrade and, if so, in what year?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did complete the academy in 1982 in Belgrade. That's when I graduated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in 1982, upon completing the academy in Belgrade, sir, were you commissioned in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was. I was given the title of lieutenant, the rank of lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And upon graduation from the military academy in Belgrade, did you undertake any additional military training or undertake any specialised military training?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: After I graduated I joined the 52nd Corps of the former Yugoslavia in Pristina, and I was platoon commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, how long did you remain with the 52nd Corps of the JNA in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I was there from 1982 until 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And other than being a platoon commander of the military police, what other assignments did you hold in that period from 1982 through 1989?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I was company commander and finally, in 1987, battalion commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So during that entire period from 1982 through 1989 you were assigned military police duties; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, after 1989, can you tell us what your next military assignment was with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: In February 1989, I moved to the military technical school in Zagreb, and I was an assistant teacher in war skills.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And for how long did you remain in this position at the military technical school in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Until October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what happened in October 1991 in terms of your professional career?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Before October 1991, I had contacts with the democratically elected government of the Republic of Croatia, and since the aggression against my country had started, I cooperated with that government. And in October 1991, I left the centre of the technical school and joined the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier Biskic, let me ask you this. There was reference on page 10, line 9 and 10, where you indicated "the aggression against my country had started." Which country are you referring to when you say "my country"?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: The Republic of Croatia, because I was living in Croatia at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, were you born in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I was born in Derventa, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you explain how in October 1991 you came to consider Croatia to be -- or the Republic of Croatia to be your country?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Because I am a Croat and my family lived in Croatia, my wife and my child.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you tell us, upon joining the army of the Republic of Croatia in October 1991, what were your duties?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I was in the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, and I worked to prepare the organisation and establishment of the military police, and at the beginning of December, after the military police was established and the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, I was appointed chief of the department of the general military police and the traffic police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And how can did you remain as the chief of the department of the general military police and the traffic police?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Until June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did there come a time, sir, when you in your official capacities within the army of the Republic of Croatia received any requests for assistance from the HVO in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: As I was born on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I had contacts with the -- my family living in Posavina -- or, rather, Derventa, my extended family, and I learnt about the situation through them, through my contacts with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say you learned about the situation, can you give us an approximate time period that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say "the situation," can you be more specific or elaborate on what the situation was in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Well, in 1992 is when the aggression of the former army started, and the members of, if I can put it this way, part of the Serbian people in territories inhabited by Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Brigadier Biskic, do you recall approximately when you first heard of the HVO as an organised force?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I think that was sometime in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And did you receive, sir, any requests for assistance from the HVO in your official capacity with the army of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: No, not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you at any point after April 1992 receive such requests?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Well, already in May 1992 I already maintained certain contacts with members of the Croatian Defence Council from the Posavina area, and through the 72nd Battalion of the military police operational in Split we learnt that the military police of the Croatian Defence Council was under establishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And upon learning that the military police of the HVO was under establishment, what steps, if any, did the military police of the republic of the army of Croatia undertake?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Well, after I learnt about that, I don't know in what way, but we came into contact with the chief of the department of the military police of the Croatian Defence Council, and that was Mr. Valentin Coric, and I think that was the second half of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, sir, that you came into contact with Mr. Coric, can you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly when we met or whether we talked over the phone, but he had contacts with my chief of department, Mr. Lausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you privy, sir, or did you at any point in time learn what were the subject of these contacts or discussions between Mr. Lausic and Mr. Coric?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I think that we took part in these talks together later on when we met, and mostly it related to the -- to assistance in the establishment of the military police of the Croatian Defence Council and conveying our experience in the establishment of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you give us some examples, sir, of the type of assistance that was provided from the Republic of Croatia army to the HVO military police?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that it was at the beginning of June that we found ourselves on the territory of Herzegovina. I think we met in Grude with the chief of the department of the military police of the Croatian Defence Council, Mr. Valentin Coric. I think that's where we met.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall any specific types of assistance that was requested?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Well, we discussed the establishment of the military police, and we gave certain instructions for how the military police was to work, of course, those aspects that did not -- were not marked secret, and I think at that first stage part of the military -- we gave them some military police equipment such as truncheons and white belts and some other equipment and clothing and other logistics -- logistical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, what other type of logistical equipment might have been supplied during this time period in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I believe that those were supplies, torches, sleeping bags, and similar military police equipment. I don't think that we provided member with any weapons at the time. Not we as the administration of the military police of the Ministry of the Interior [as interpreted] of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, other than this meeting that you believe occurred in Grude, did you have any other meetings that included Mr. Coric in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes. We were together in Posavina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, sir. Maybe this is a mistake in the transcript, in the translation of your words. In line -- on page 14, line 3, you're talking about the -- the administration of the military police of the Ministry of the Interior. The military police in Croatia, was it under the Ministry of the Interior or the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not say the administration of the military police was with the Ministry of the Interior but, rather, that it was with the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia. The military police was not under the Ministry of the Interior but under the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I just wanted to clarify this. Page 14, line 3, it should say "Ministry of Defence." Mr. Mundis, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This meeting, sir, that occurred in Posavina, do you recall approximately when that meeting was and who attended?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I believe that this was sometime in June 1992. I don't remember the exact date. Those who were commanders of military police platoons in Posavina attended. I believe that the commander of the operations group of eastern Posavina, Mr. Stefanek was there as well, Mr. Valentin Coric, myself, and I can't recall who else was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, Brigadier Biskic, approximately -- for approximately how long this assistance from the Republic of Croatia army military police to the HVO military police lasted?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: The military police of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia in the course of the entire period in one way or another assisted the military police of the HVO in the organisation of their work by conveying their experiences and by providing them with military police equipment. And sometime as of 1993 onwards, we also educated military policemen or helped with the education of military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me, sir, ask you two follow-on questions. You just told us on the -- line 9 of page 15, "in the course of the entire period." Can you please tell us what you meant by "the course of the entire period"?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the period of the Homeland War, which took place between 1992 and 1995 and even after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us, sir, also, on page 15 at lines 12 and 13, "We also educated military policemen or helped with the education of military policemen," and I'm wondering if you can give us some examples of what you mean by education or educating military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: When I said that we educated military policemen, I meant the courses that we organised for traffic policemen, general policemen, also assistance with the training of crime police officers, because in the armed forces I -- in the military police of the Republic of Croatia we had an education centre where we trained all military policemen starting with foot soldiers to non-commissioned officers as well as commissioned officers affiliated with the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask if the usher could please provide the bundle of documents that has been prepared for use with this witness. I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you if could please turn to the first document in that bundle, which is P 05001, and I would ask you, sir, if you've ever seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document refers to, please?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: This is a request by the military police of the Croatian Defence Council to provide education for police officers on motorcycles and follows a list of 10 members of the Croatian Defence Council who are being sent for a training course in the education centre of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, Brigadier Biskic, the training centre or the education centre of the military police, where was this education centre that you've referred to? Where was this located?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: The training centre of the military police of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia was in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Now, I'd like to turn with you to different topic, sir, and that is a meeting that you had in November, 1993, with General Bobetko. Do you remember that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember the specific date of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: The 6th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at that point in time, Brigadier Biskic, 6 November 1993, what position did you hold in the army of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I was the deputy chief of administration of the military police of the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on 6 November 1993, sir, what position did General Bobetko hold?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: General Bobetko was the chief of the Main Staff of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, approximately what time on 6 November 1993 this meeting took place and where?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I believe that the meeting took place in the evening in the meeting room of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This was in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: In Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Other than yourself, sir, and General Bobetko, who was in attendance at this meeting on 6 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: General Bobetko's assistants General Agotic; General Lucic; General Roso; Brigadier Crnjac; Brigadier Vrbanac; Major Butorac; Major Ljubo Cesic, Rojs; and I can't recall any of the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you've just provided a few names and ranks of individuals. Can you tell us in which armed force or armed forces the persons you've just mentioned were serving?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: The armed forces of the Republic of Croatia, i.e., the Croatian forces. And there was also General Tole from the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you recall, Brigadier Biskic, what General Bobetko told this group of officers that included yourself on 6 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: General Bobetko informed us about the very complex situation in the territories under the control of the Croatian Defence Council, especially in Bosnia in Croatian enclaves - those were -- those were the zones of responsibility of the HVO there - and he said that they decided to accepted us to assist the Croatian Defence Council with a view to carrying out an operation of joining up the HVO forces on the Uskoplje-Vitez axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall any of the specifics about the very complex situation that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: General Tole provided an overview of the situation, spoke about the offences carried out by the Muslim forces in the territory of Central Bosnia. He spoke about the lack of ammunition and food in the area of Central Bosnia, and in general terms he spoke about the problems in the system of the control and command in the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know Brigadier Biskic, at this point in time, that is 6 November 1993, what position General Tole had in the Croatian Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I believe that he was the Chief of Staff in the Main Staff of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, anything else General Bobetko told you at this meeting on 6 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Mostly we spoke about the situation and the need to help the Croatian Defence Council both by sharing our experience that we gained in the Croatian army, and, judging by who attended the meeting, we were of different specialties and we belonged to different branches of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us a few moments ago as reflected on page 18, lines 17 and 18, that General Tole mentioned problems in the system of command and control in the Croatian Defence Council, and I'm wondering if you can elaborate upon that or perhaps be more specific about what you recall being said in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: He didn't say anything specific. He did not illustrate anything. He spoke in general terms about problems and the situation in the HVO, and also that they would need assistance from a certain number of the officers of the Croatian army who were born on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say they would need assistance from a certain number of officers of the Croatian army, did that include the group of officers that was present in General Bobetko's office on that evening, 6 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is specifically who I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Other than yourself, sir, were there any of the other individuals who were present at this meeting who had a background in military police or military police administration?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I was the only one with MP experience at that meeting, and I believe that General Tole in the former military also was a member of the military police for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, what rank you held in the Republic of Croatia army on 6 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: At the moment I was a colonel, and I was to be promoted into the rank of brigadier. The proposal was put forward in August 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Following this meeting on 6 November 1993 that you've told us about, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I returned home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And did you in fact after this meeting travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went to Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 8th of November. I arrived in Posusje sometime in the afternoon of that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: On the 8th of November, I -- let me ask you this, sir: This is 8 November 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Correct. The 8th of November, 1993. In the afternoon I arrived in Posusje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on that day, sir, did you travel by yourself or with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: A number of officers together with General Roso flew there. We took regular Croatia airlines slight to Split, and from Split we were given there by cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say, Brigadier Biskic, a number of officers together with General Roso, do you recall who those officers were that travelled with you on 8 November 1993 on the flight to Split?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: General Roso, Colonel Dumancic, Major Butorac, Major Ljubo Cesic, Rojs, Brigadier Vrbanac, Brigadier Crnjac. I believe that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, sir, in which armed force or armed forces were these officers serving on 8 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: They were members of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia, and I believe that they were all born in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, you have to understand that up to 1991 we all lived in one state, and that when the aggression started against the Republic of Croatia, Croats from Bosnia-Herzegovina participated in the Republic of Croatia as volunteers. When the aggression started against their own homes, some of them had already returned to the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, even before that. So that then and now I believe that it was only normal for us to go and help the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Brigadier Biskic, among the group of officers from the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia that travelled with you on 8 November 1993, was one of those persons in charge or in command?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: General Roso.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, sir, so that we're very clear, what position did General Roso hold on the 8th of November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in the territory of the Croatian Defence Council in Posusje, he said that he was appointed the chief of the General Staff of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll get to that in just a moment, sir. Let me try this: On the 7th of November, 1993, what position did General Roso hold?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I can't remember what position he held in the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia, but I believe that he was the assistant for special units of the Main Staff. However, I can't be sure of that. Since I did not work in the Main Staff but, rather, in the Ministry of Defence, and I really testimony not know the exact position that General Roso held at the time, and I still don't know it to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Brigadier Biskic, about the structure of the HVO at the time you arrived in Bosnia-Herzegovina on 8 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, could you please be more specific? When you say "structure," what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's start with, to the extent you know, can you tell us about the military side of the HVO, the armed forces of the Croatian Defence Council as it was structured at the time of your arrival in Bosnia and Herzegovina on 8 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I believe that at the time there still existed a defence department which was being transformed into the system of the Ministry of Defence, i.e., it was being organised to become the Ministry of Defence. There was also the Main Staff of the Croatian Defence Council. There were organisational units such as territories. There were also brigades of the Croatian Defence Council, and there were some operations group in the territory of Glava which were isolated. There were also units of the military police of the Croatian Defence Council. That would be just the basic outline of the structure that existed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, let's -- let me ask you some follow-up questions from what you've just told us. This defence department that was in the process of being transformed into a ministry of defence, testimony your arrival, sir, who was in charge of that department or ministry?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I said that it was undergoing transformation. When I arrived down there, there already existed the Ministry of Defence, and that was Mr. Perica Jukic, and from that I inferred that the reorganisation of the department of defence was underway.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Brigadier Biskic, do you know who Bruno Stojic is?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What position, if any, did he hold within the HVO government at the time of your arrival in Bosnia and Herzegovina on 8 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether Mr. Bruno Stojic held a position at the time. Before that he was the head of the defence department. Perica Jukic took over from him. And at the moment I arrived, I don't think he played any role, that he held any position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned a few moments ago the Main Staff of the Croatian Defence Council. On 8 November 1993, at the time of your arrival in Bosnia and Herzegovina, who was commanding the Main Staff of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I believe that General Slobodan Praljak was the head of the Main Staff. I don't know whether he was the chief of that body or the commander. I really wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you've also told us, sir, that there were units of the military police of the Croatian Defence Council. Do you know who was responsible or in charge or in command of the military police units of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: The military police of the Croatian Defence Council, the military police administration was at the head of it, and that was within the defence department. And there was the chief at the head of the administration, and that head was Mr. Valentin Coric.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I neglected to ask you when we were talking about the Main Staff, do you know who was General Slobodan Praljak's deputy within the Main Staff of the HVO on 8 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I think it was General Milivoj Petkovic as the deputy, General Praljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know or did you have reason to learn about the structure on the government side of the HVO, that is, the non-military leadership within the government of the HVO on or about 8 November 1993 when you arrived in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't say. I can't tell you about that because I didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you don't know, sir, who was responsible in terms of the HVO government, who the leaders were, the president or Prime Minister?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I didn't say I didn't know who the Prime Minister was. I said I didn't know what the organisational establishment was like of the overall Croatian Defence Council. Of course, the Prime Minister was Mr. Prlic at the time, and the president of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was Mr. Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier Biskic, you've mentioned to us about the reorganisation within the defence department. Can you please turn to what should be the next document in the bundle, 7236. That is P 07236. Have you seen this document before, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- can you tell us what this document is, please?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: That is decision on the foundation of the establishment of the Ministry of Defence for Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what, sir, if you can succinctly tell us, what is the purpose of this document? What does this document do?

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we please have some kind of foundation that the witness is competent to answer that question? It just seems that he's being asked to speculate without any foundation as to how he would know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Brigadier Biskic, do you recall when the first time you saw this document was?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I saw it in December 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall the circumstances under which you came to see this document?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: At the time I was appointed by the Prime Minister, Mr. Prlic, as assistant minister for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us within what ministry you were appointed as assistant minister for security?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Assistant minister for security in the defence ministry of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, this position that you were appointed to by Dr. Prlic in November -- or, sorry, December 1993, is the position that you held referred to in this document?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is mentioned, because this is the decision on the foundation of the organisation of the Ministry of Defence, which prescribes how the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna is to be organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask you, sir, if you could briefly or quickly look through this document and indicate which article or provision of this document refers to the position to which you were appointed.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Article 4, the ministry decision mentions the assistant minister for security. Article 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We'll return to December and your appointment a little bit later this afternoon. Let me now turn, sir, to -- back to 8 November 1993. You told us that you arrived in Posusje. Can you tell us what was located in that town on 8 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: In that town from that time the Main Staff of the Croatian Defence Council was supposed to be displaced from Citluk to Posusje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in fact was the Main Staff of the HVO in Posusje at that time when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I think it was still in Citluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you arrived in Bosnia and Herzegovina on 8 November 1993, were you assigned to any specific duties?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: General Roso gave me an assignment by which I was his security assistant and assistant for the military police. He conveyed this to me orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier Biskic, at the time General Roso conveyed this oral order to you, what position was he holding on 8 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I've already said that at the time he said he was chief of the Main Staff of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at that point in time, what position did General Praljak hold?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I think at the time General Praljak was relieved of his duties, but I didn't actually see the papers stating that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did there ever come a time, sir, when you were shown papers to that effect, or you saw official documents to that effect?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: You mean on the relieving of duty of General Praljak?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At the time General Roso became the commander of the HVO Main Staff, did he have a deputy?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Well, later on I became aware of the fact that General Milivoj Petkovic, as deputy head of the Main Staff of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what about General Tole? What position did he hold, if you know, on or about the 8th of November, 1993, after this turnover of command?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I did not know what post he occupied, but I think he was head of the staff. Not head of staff in -- in the sense that General Roso was later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you explain that answer, sir? When you say, "not the head of the staff in the sense that General Roso was later on," can you explain what you mean by that answer, please?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that before that it was the commander of the Croatian Defence Council, a post that was performed by Mr. Praljak, the deputy was General Petkovic, and the Chief of Staff was General Tole. I didn't see those documents, but that's what rumour had it. Later on, with the arrival of General Roso, you had the Main Staff and the chief of the Main Staff had his deputy, and within the staff you had the various departments, administrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, on 8 November 1993 when you arrived in Bosnia-Herzegovina, what type of uniform were you wearing?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what type of insignia did you have on your uniform?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: At the time I had the Croatian Defence Council insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Prior to that day, sir, prior to the 8th of November, 1993, what insignia did you wear on your uniform?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Before that I was in the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia, and I had the Croatian army insignia and the military police insignia of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Brigadier Biskic, can you tell us how you changed the insignia on your uniform at the time you went to Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Well, quite simply. The Croatian army had just a patch, a velcro patch, so I took the velcro patch off and put on the HVO velcro patch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, what insignia the other officers from the army of the Republic of Croatia were wearing at the time of their arrival with you in Bosnia and Herzegovina? I'm talking about the group that travelled with you; what insignia did they have on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Some had uniforms, others wore civilian clothing, but by the time we were down there everybody was wearing uniforms with the Croatian Defence Council insignia and patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier Biskic, can you tell us, after your arrival on 8 November 1993, how long did you remain on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I remained until the 6th of May, 1994. At the time, there was a two-month interruption from the 28th of January until the 25th of March, because my wife was ill. So I went back to Zagreb and was on leave during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, during that time period, sir, from 25 January until 25 March 1994, did you at any point in time in that approximately two month period return to Bosnia and Herzegovina and, if so, when?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: From the 23rd to the 25th of February I was there because in those days the Defence Minister changed, and instead of Mr. Perica Jukic the Defence minister became Mr. Vladimir Soljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, for the rest of the direct examination when I'm referring to the period you were in Bosnia and Herzegovina, I'm referring to the period from 8 November 1993 until 6th of May, 1994. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And by no means am I trying to trick you. We all understand from the 25th of January until the 25th of March, 1994 -- or the 28th of January until the 25th of March, 1994, you were not in Bosnia-Herzegovina with the exception of the 23rd to 25th of February. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier Biskic, during the time period that you were in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where were you drawing your salary from?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: First of all, if you refer to me as brigadier, could you refer to me as brigadier -- retired brigadier, because it's not the same thing. If you say "Brigadier Biskic," that's one thing, and if you say "retired brigadier," that's another. So could you do that, please? And I received my salary in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And which -- which government was paying your salary?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: The government of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, when did you ultimately leave the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: On the 31st of December, 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at any point in time, sir, from October 1991 through the end of December 2005, did you resign or otherwise give up your commission in the army of Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: No. My involvement within the territory of the Croatian Defence Council was in the form of assistance of the Republic of Croatia to the Croatian people on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And if you're giving assistance to somebody, if you're helping somebody, then I considered it normal that that assistance should not be paid for or, rather, that I should not receive a salary down there for providing that assistance. And my family lived in Zagreb, so it was logical that I received my salary in Croatia. The Republic of Croatia in its constitution tied up this question of assistance to -- regulated the matter of assistance to Croatians on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That is regulated under the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you, sir, at any point in time while you were in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina receive any form of payment from Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. I'm about to move into a different subject. I'm wondering if this might be an appropriate time for the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite. We're going to take a 20-minute break and reconvene in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A question, or, rather, an answer before the next question from the Prosecutor, if I may be allowed. You said that I was here as a Prosecution witness. I am here pursuant to a court order, and I'm testifying about the period of time that I worked in. I had no preparations either today or yesterday because I just arrived yesterday at around 1300 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When I said that you were a Prosecution witness, it was because we are in a proceedings by which the Prosecutor calls witnesses and so does the Defence. The Defence calls witnesses, too. Now, since you have taken the solemn declaration, you are a witness of the court and justice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me ask you this: When you first arrived in Bosnia and Herzegovina on the 8th of November, 1993, and for the rest of the month of November 1993, what were your duties and responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: My duties and responsibilities upon my arrival on the territory of the Croatian Defence Council or the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna were, in the first stage, geared towards the preparation and organisation of the military police and the security and information service, intelligence service, in Uskoplje and Central Bosnia, that general area. Later on in the course of November, since the Ministry of Defence was being organised and established, at the meetings that were held at the level of the Ministry of Defence and the Main Staff, it was decided that I should be the person to coordinate the work of SIS and the military police administration, which were -- already at that time was the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, and that in the course of November a decision would be made as to my concrete post within the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, when you told us that you were involved in the preparation and organisation of the military police and security and information service, what exactly were you doing?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: From the very beginning I said that I coordinated the work of the military police and the security and information or intelligence services in preparation of operations, and later on during November, through my work and through receiving reports from the head of SIS, Mr. Ivica Lucic, who was the acting chief of the military police department, Mr. Radoslav Lavric, I appraised the situation in the military police and in SIS and prepared, to the with my staff, the new establishment of the military police of the Croatian Defence Council and the security and information service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, based on this appraisal of the situation in the military police and in the SIS, can you tell the Trial Chamber about the situation that you found with respect to the military police and the SIS in terms of how they were functioning and how they were operating?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: When I arrived, the administration of the military police of the Croatian Defence Council was working within the composition of the defence department as it had been up till then, and it comprised of several departments or sections, and the military police battalions were operational at the level of the then military districts. The battalion of the military police for south-east Herzegovina, Central Bosnia, Posavina, and north-east. And attached to each of these military districts there was a Light Assault Battalion and the military police platoons working under the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, what was the relationship between the military police and the Light Assault Battalion that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: The Light Assault Battalions of the military police were a component part of the military police in the Croatian Defence Council, but they were focused on involvement and assignments within combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber about the quality of the command and control structures within the military police administration of the HVO at the time you arrived on 8 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: According to the reports and in talking to the heads of the department of the military police or, rather, the acting head, Mr. Lavric, and meetings that we had in the Main Staff and the defence ministry, it was said that there were problems in the system of control and command because the military police units were involved up at the front line mostly and were not able to be engaged in executing their regular tasks or, rather, the regular military police assignments. Furthermore, it was also noted that there were problems with respect to command over the platoons of the military police within the brigades. Although they were supposed to be within the chain of command of the military police, this very often was not the case in practice. And it was also noted that there were problems in cooperation between the civilian police on the military police. Then there was not a high level of cooperation between the SIS and the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, how did these problems that you've identified impact upon the military police of the HVO in terms of carrying out its mission or functions?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: It's very difficult to answer this question. I said that there were some problems and weaknesses in the work because the military police for the most part was on the front line and to a lesser extent they were performing regular police duties. They were also engaged in the control of entry at the border crossings between Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as on other duties that were supposed to pertain within the purview of the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were the military police units of the HVO functional or dysfunctional in November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: To a certain extent, yes, and to another extent no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you explain, please, what you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: This means that if most of the military police are engaged on the front line, then they don't perform well in their normal policing work such as the control of security in the territory under the control of the HVO, prevention of crime, and other such things that they would normally do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, sir, what happened with respect to the position that you held on the 1st of December, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you -- did you, sir, assume a new position on 1 December 1993, and, if so, what position did you assume?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 1st of December, 1993, the president of the government, Mr. Jadranko Prlic, appointed me as assistant minister for security in the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you please turn to the document tabbed 6994 in the bundle in front of you. 6994. That's P 06994. Sir, have you seen this document before and, if so, can you tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw this document until December 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what is -- what is this document?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: This is a decision by which I was appointed the assistant minister of defence for security, and this is signed by the president by the HR HB government, Dr. Jadranko Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you please turn, sir, to the next document in your bundle, P 06998, 6998. Mr. Biskic, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I saw it when I spoke to you and before that in December 1993. I didn't see it when I stayed in the territory of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna because I did not read the Official Gazette at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you just tell us, however, what this Article 1 -- or the first decision on this page relates to?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: This refers to my appointment as the assistant minister of defence for security issues in the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Biskic, can you please tell us about the functions that you performed as the assistant minister for security within the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: As the assistant minister for security, I was superior to the chief of the traffic police and the chief of information police that were part of the security sector of the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what types of duties did you undertake in this role?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: This means that I was in a way responsible and superior to the chiefs of various administrations for all military police tasks and the tasks of information services and their purview of work -- MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that we have an error in transcript. In line 22, page 36, the traffic police was mentioned and this was omitted from the translation. Maybe my learned friend Mr. Mundis should check whether this is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps there is some confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, as the assistant minister for security, were you superior to the chief of the traffic police?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: No, no traffic police. When I said the administration of the military police, I said that there was a department of traffic police. The traffic police of the Croatian Defence Council consisted of general police, traffic police, crime prevention police. Those were the three speciality within the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe for us who reported to you in your capacity as the assistant minister for security within the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna? What were the functional titles of the persons and the names of the persons holding those positions?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: People who reported to me were the chiefs of administration of military police and the administration for security and information. From the 11th of November, 1993, up to the beginning of January 1994, there was no chief of the military police. There was just an acting chief, and that was Mr. Radoslav Lavric. And the chief of the administration for security information was Mr. Ivica Lucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, sir, whom did Mr. Radoslav Lavric replace as the chief of the military police administration on 11 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Up to then, and I don't know whether this was on the 11th of November or the 10th of November, Mr. Valentin Coric was appointed the minister of the interior of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. His deputy up to then was Mr. Radoslav Lavric, and during the course of November he performed the duty as the deputy and then he was appointed the acting chief of the MP administration of the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me just ask you one other series of questions before we talk a little bit more about your duties in December 1993, and that has to do with how well the officers from the army of Republic of Croatia were received by members of the HVO armed forces. Can you comment on that, the situation that you faced?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: When we arrived, we were given our working space. As far as I'm personally concerned, I did not have any problems at the beginning or later when working with the officers of the HVO with whom I had to work and with whom I met there upon my arrival.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's turn then, sir, to December 1993 and the period onward after you had assumed the position of assistant minister for security. What were the primary accomplishments that were made during the time period that you were the assistant minister of security?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the entire period, Mr. Prosecutor, or are you referring just to the November/December period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let's start with the November/December period as a starting point. What were the main accomplishments that you made in November, December 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: During the month of November 1993, during the period when I was not appointed the assistant minister, I looked at the situation in the military police, in the Security Information Service. I informed myself about the scope of work and authorities and competencies, and then I was informed about collection centres and centres for prisoner of war. And together with others, I participated in the work of the Main Staff and Ministry of Defence in the preparation for passing documentation and in the preparations for the reorganisation of the Croatian Defence Council that was to follow later on. At first I participated in the preparation for the operation in the territory of Uskoplje. I determined the role of the military police and the -- and security services in that operation. We passed rules of engagement during that operation for both these services, and I prepared the new organisation of the security information services and the military police that came into effect in December when people were selected and when there were shakeups to a greater extent in the military police and to a lesser extent in the information service. In the course of November I learned about problems in collection centres and the place where prisoners of war were accommodated in Heliodrom. I proposed certain measures to the chief of the Main Staff and the Ministry of Defence in order to improve the conditions of accommodation, the life and work of the detainees.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, we'll take a number of the things you've just mentioned in turn, but let me ask you this: Upon your arrival in Bosnia and Herzegovina in November 1993, what kind of reporting system was in place with respect to the activities of the military police within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Since I arrived to take a duty that was not occupied by anybody before that, I did not receive any documentation. I did not take over any documentation for anybody. I did not carry out a detailed analysis of the system of reporting either in the military police or from the military police to other participants in the system of reporting, and I never analysed the system of reporting from the -- in the security services or from the security services to the officials of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. I asked for an overview of the situation both in the military police and in the security services, and based on that I introduced a system of reporting, reporting to me from the chief of the administrations for military police and security services and towards other officials in the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna and above them at higher positions. I also issued documents in order to regulate relationship between the security services and the military police in order to provide for a better cooperation and better reporting, as well as coordination between those two services.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, this system of reporting that you told us that you introduced from the chief of administrations for military police and security services, can you tell us a little bit more about how those reports were produced, the frequency of those reports, and to whom those reports were distributed?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I believe that at the time on the 17th of November I introduced the first bulletin about the events where the military police was engaged, and I also introduced the system of the reports of the security services about the situation of security in the territory of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. Such reports arrived at my desk as assistant minister, and in November already, as assistant chief of the Main Staff in the security system, and also to the other addressees within the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, i.e., the Main Staff of the Croatian Defence Council, the billeting of the military police was also sent to the addressees that were higher above to the military prosecutor's office and military courts, the president of the government, and the president of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What type of information was included in these bulletins and how were they physically produced or who produced them and based upon what?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Daily reports that were drafted by the military police administration of the Croatian Defence Council were based on the daily reports of the military police units in the territory of the Croatian Defence Council, and this was all based on the interventions of the military police when it came to the disruption of peace or the regulation and control of road traffic or crime that was investigated by the military police or other activities, daily activities that the military police had to perform during the 24 hours reporting period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, could you please turn to the next exhibit in your bundle, which is marked 6722. That's P 06722. Do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell it us what this document is, please?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: This is a daily report of the military police administration of the Croatian Defence Council. It is entitled "Bulletin number 2," or in other words, bulletin, and before me I have document number 2, dated 18 November 1993, which means that the first bulletin was issued on the 18th [as interpreted] of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps there's -- perhaps there's an error in the English transcript. It says, "which means that the first bulletin was issued on the 18th of November, 1993." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: The 17th November 1993 is the date of the first one, because the 18th of November was the date when the second bulletin was issued under number 2. The first one was on the 17th of November, the second one on the 18th, number three on the 19th, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, perhaps you can just answer this question very quickly for us. Next to the date on the bottom of this document, on the first page of this document, it indicates a reference to Ljubuski. Can you tell us why this document apparently was produced in Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: The seat of the MP administration of the Croatian Defence Council was in Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And at this point in time, sir, that is in mid-November 1993, where were you physically working?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: I was in Posusje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Biskic, a few moments ago you mentioned in some detail some of the steps you took in terms of organisation and establishment of the military police or re-establishment of the military police. Can you tell us in a little more detail about the steps you took in terms of organising or re-organising the military police of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: At the beginning of December the Minister of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Perica Jukic, at my proposal and an agreement with the chief of the Main Staff of the Croatian Defence Council, General Roso, signed an order on the reorganisation of the military police of the Croatian Defence Council. This order in a certain way was preceded by the preparations for the reorganisation that took place in the course of November 1993. The reorganisation itself was launched and was due to the preparations for the reorganisation of the Croatian Defence Council and awareness that a new organisation is required in the new times and in the new stages of the development of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, what do you mean by the awareness that a new organisation is required in the new times and in the new stages of the development? What -- what do you mean by that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: What I am saying is that every stage in the development of the Croatian Defence Council called for the adjustment of the organisation in the Croatian Defence Council. When General Roso be -- came to the position of the Chief of the General Staff of the Croatian Defence Council was the time when the Croatian Defence Council started being reorganised, and before that the military police of the Croatian Defence Council was reorganised as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you turn it, sir, to document 7018, P 07018. Can you tell us what this document is, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: This is an order by the minister of defence, Mr. Perica Jukic, on the reorganisation of the military police of the Croatian Defence Council. The date is 3rd December 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Biskic, is this the document that you just mentioned a moment ago that was based upon a proposal that you had put forward?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us in a -- in a nutshell or very succinctly what the main components or the main facets of the reorganisation that you propose and which is reflected in P 07018 would be?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC
utterances.text: Under item 1 of this order you can see that units of the military police are determined, their numeral signs, where they are to be established and in which zone of responsibility are they to perform military police duties. Item 1 says that there will be a battalion of the military police of the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Defence Council with the headquarters in Mostar. The 2nd Battalion headquartered in Livno, which will perform duties in the areas of responsibilities of the Territorial Defence -- of the territorial districts of Tomislavgrad, Posusje, Prozor, and one platoon of the military police in Uskoplje. And that is how other units are defined, such as the 3rd Battalion headquartered in Citluk with its task in the zone of Mostar. Also, companies are determined in Siroki Brijeg, Capljina, Ljubuski, Stolac. Within the 3rd Battalion were military police platoons in Buna and Neum. Further on under 1.4 it says that a company of the military police is formed to provide security for the prisoners of war in the military investigative prison headquartered in Heliodrom in Mostar. Also, there will be a teaching company of the military police for the -- for the training of recruits of the military police with headquarters in Capljina. And in Vitez. It says Kiseljak here. This was only an operations group. The Orasje, and also an operations group was in Zepce where independent companies of the military police are established. In -- in item 2 it is ordered that platoons of the military police shall no longer be part of the brigades of the HVO but of the 2nd and 3rd battalions of the Croatian Defence Council, which means that both troops and their equipment will be transferred. In item 3 it is said that members of the military police in the brigades who do not wish to join the military police companies shall return the military police equipment and join the brigades, and when they do that they stop being military policemen.
